entries.title: Psalms 73:1
segments:
. Of Asaph--(see (unresolved link)). God is good to His people. For although the prosperity of the wicked, and the afflictions of the righteous, tempted the Psalmist to misgivings of God's government, yet the sudden and fearful ruin of the ungodly, seen in the light of God's revelation, reassures his heart; and, chiding himself for his folly, he is led to confide renewedly in God, and celebrate His goodness and love.

) describes the true Israel.

entries.title: Psalms 73:10
segments: 10-12. Hence God's people are confounded, turned hither (or back) and thither, perplexed with doubts of God's knowledge and care, and filled with sorrow.

entries.title: Psalms 73:12
segments: 12. prosper in the word--literally, "secure for ever."

entries.title: Psalms 73:13
segments: 13, 14. The Psalmist, partaking of these troubles, is especially disturbed in view of his own case, that with all his diligent efforts for a holy life, he is still sorely tried.

entries.title: Psalms 73:15
